solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Service area with major retail chain strikes out

definitions.note: cancels, as an order is cancelled

parts.note: a counter is where customers are served in a shop or bank
M and S, Marks and Spencer, a big British department-store chain

explanation.surface: A motorway services with a big store chain has its staff walking out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service area' suggests a motorway stop, but it is a shop counter. M&S (Marks and Spencer) is a major British retail chain, here spelt out as M AND S.
explanation.definitionFit: To countermand an order is to revoke it, cancelling or striking it out.

clue.text: Sort of bomb left in possession of US general

indicators.note: in possession of means the general holds the abbreviation for left

parts.note: George Custer, the US general of Little Bighorn

explanation.surface: A bomb was left with an American general.
explanation.definitionFit: A cluster bomb scatters many small bomblets over an area.

clue.text: Woman, jolly journalist, incapable of giving offence

parts.note: Una is a woman's name
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, RM
ed, editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A cheerful woman journalist who would never upset anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' reads as cheerful but is old naval slang for a Royal Marine (RM).
explanation.definitionFit: Unarmed means carrying no weapons, so unable to attack: offence here is attack, not insult.

clue.text: Cutting earthwork to shelter soldier?

parts.note: a trench is a dug earthwork
a soldier ant is a kind of ant, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A trench is dug to protect a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to shelter' describes what a trench does for the soldier; the pieces simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant means incisive and sharp, as a cutting remark is.

clue.text: Laughing Cavalier in art

indicators.note: cavalier means offhand and careless, so the letters are treated carelessly and rearranged

explanation.surface: The Laughing Cavalier, the famous Frans Hals portrait, appears in art.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hides the title of the painting; 'Cavalier' is the anagram signal on IN ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Riant is a literary word, from French, for smiling or cheerful.

clue.text: Gather a quantity of leaves round about

indicators.note: round means the first pieces go round the abbreviation for about

parts.note: a quire is a measure of paper, 24 or 25 sheets
c, circa, means about

explanation.surface: Gather up a heap of fallen leaves round about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' are sheets of paper, not foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire is to get or collect, as one gathers things.

clue.text: Dull, collecting yokel's top and bottom separately at the end

indicators.note: separately says the yokel's bottom goes into the dull word at a different place from the top
collecting means the word for dull takes in the yokel's letters

parts.note: dingy means drab and dull

indicators.note: top picks the first letter of the yokel

parts.note: the bottom of the yokel is its last letter, L

explanation.surface: A dull yokel is gathered up at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'separately' tells you the two letters, Y and L, go into DINGY at different points: Y after the D, L before the final Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyingly means in the manner of one dying, at the very end of life.

clue.text: Sports ground masks label on international competitors

indicators.note: masks means the shuffled letters cover up the other pieces
ground means the letters of sports are ground up and reformed

parts.note: a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A sports ground hides a label placed on an international player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' is the past tense of grind, not a sports field: it rearranges SPORTS, which then masks TAG ON I.
explanation.definitionFit: Protagonists are leading participants or contestants in a struggle, competitors.

clue.text: Having hand in decadent fancy dish

indicators.note: in places the word for hand inside the word for decadent

parts.note: a roue is a decadent, dissolute man
a lad is a hand, as in a stable lad or farm hand

explanation.surface: A dissolute gourmet has a hand in preparing some extravagant dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decadent' is a noun here: a roue, a debauched man.
explanation.definitionFit: A roulade is a rolled, filled dish, sweet or savoury, a showy piece of cookery.

clue.text: See 10
Maybe Hoover vacuum cleaner left dust around politician once

definitions.note: the full name of a past British prime minister

parts.note: Herbert Hoover, US president, is one Herbert
Henry is a popular British brand of vacuum cleaner with a smiling face

indicators.note: around means the word for dust goes round the word for left

parts.note: ash is a fine dust left by burning
quit means left, departed

explanation.surface: A Hoover vacuum cleaner gathers dust around a politician of former days.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun is on Hoover: first the president's first name, then the brand that makes vacuum cleaners suggests another cleaner, the British Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Henry Asquith was the Liberal prime minister of Britain from 1908 to 1916.

clue.text: Iconic organisation for the better means to pick up what's said

parts.note: the Tote is the British betting organisation; the better here is one who bets

parts.words: means to pick up what's said
parts.note: a mic, a microphone, picks up speech

explanation.surface: A body devoted to improvement deploys some device for catching spoken words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the better' reads as an improvement but means a bettor, one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: Totemic means serving as an emblem or symbol, which is what iconic also means.

clue.text: Tango with scaffolder friend of 'Dave'

parts.note: Tango is T in the radio alphabet
a rigger is a worker who puts up scaffolding

explanation.surface: A dancing scaffolder is pals with someone called Dave.
explanation.walkthrough: In the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses, the slow-witted road sweeper Trigger always calls Rodney 'Dave', hence the quotes.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitcom character Trigger is the friend who insists on calling Rodney by the wrong name, Dave.

clue.text: Wounded, become bloody

parts.note: to go is to become, as in go mad
red is the colour of blood

explanation.surface: Someone injured and now covered in blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Gored means pierced and wounded by a horn or tusk.

clue.text: Smart sports car model

parts.note: arch means knowing and clever, slyly smart
the E-type is a classic Jaguar sports car

explanation.surface: A chic sports car serves as a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' reads as stylish but means arch, cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is an original model or pattern from which copies are made.

clue.text: One holds up chap with chutzpah, British ace

definitions.note: chap is the jaw or cheek, which this bone supports

parts.note: cheek is brazen nerve, chutzpah
an ace is one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: Someone holds up a cheeky British ace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chap' looks like a man but is the cheek or jaw, as in the plural chaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheekbone is the facial bone that supports the cheek beneath the eye.

clue.text: Bill's written about short dance in work of fiction

indicators.note: written about means the bill's word is set down around the dance

parts.note: a note is a bill, as in a banknote or account

indicators.note: short means the dance's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a veleta is a ballroom dance in waltz time

explanation.surface: Bill has written about a brief dance in his novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The veleta is an old-time British ballroom dance; 'short' docks its last letter, and 'written about' wraps the bill round what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelette is a short novel, often a light romantic one: a work of fiction.

clue.text: Collection of Graves? Poet finally given a bust

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters are smashed and rearranged
finally takes the last letter of poet

explanation.surface: A collection by the poet Robert Graves is finally given a sculpted bust.
explanation.walkthrough: Graves looks like the poet but is the Bordeaux wine; 'bust' breaks up T GIVEN A.
explanation.definitionFit: A vintage is the wine of one year's harvest, so a collection of Graves wine from a season.

clue.text: Long time wrapped in string like a cat

indicators.note: wrapped in means the long time sits inside the word for string

parts.note: a line is a string or cord
an eon is an immensely long time

explanation.surface: A cat spends ages tangled in a ball of string.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means like a lion, a big cat.

clue.text: Do be quiet at the back

definitions.note: used as a verb meaning cheat

parts.note: sh is the call to be quiet
aft means at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A request for silence from the back of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is slang for swindle, not the everyday helping verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To shaft someone is slang for cheating or treating them unfairly, as is to do them.

clue.text: Release from prison holding unknown number of traitors

indicators.note: holding means the word for release from prison contains the unknown

parts.note: to spring someone is to free them from jail
y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A jailbreak frees an unknown number of traitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a group, not a figure; 'unknown' gives the algebraic Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A spy ring is a group of agents working together, traitors to their country.

clue.text: I'm saint converted from primitive religion

definitions.note: an adjective, describing what belongs to that belief

indicators.note: converted means the letters are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: A saint has been converted from some primitive faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' looks religious but rearranges I'M SAINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Animism, the belief that spirits dwell in natural things, is seen as an early form of religion.

clue.text: In brief, US politician gets lift leaving party

parts.note: Sen is the short form of senator
to doff a hat is to lift it in greeting

explanation.surface: A US senator hitches a ride as he quits his party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks political but is a celebration; 'leaving' is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A send-off is a farewell gathering for someone departing.

clue.text: Scrap something insignificant that odd characters rejected

parts.note: not caring a fig: a fig is a trifle

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of that are thrown out, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Throw out a trifle that some strange people turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' reads as discard, but means a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a fight or tussle.

clue.text: Keenly working to restrict newspaper's graphic edge

indicators.note: to restrict means the shuffled letters close round the newspaper
working means the letters of keenly are put to work in a new order

parts.note: i is a British national newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone keenly labours to hold back a paper's graphic edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges KEENLY, which then holds I.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, a keyline is an outline marking the edge where a graphic or image is placed.

clue.text: Taxing heavily as a ruler

parts.note: so can mean as, as in 'so far' for 'as far'
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: Heavy taxes are just what a monarch imposes.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak someone is slang for extracting a lot of money, especially by heavy taxation.

clue.text: One enthralled by old organ player of distinction

indicators.note: enthralled by means one is held inside the old organ

parts.note: the liver is a body organ
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone captivated by an ancient church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests music, but it is the body's liver.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was among the most celebrated actors of the twentieth century, a player of great distinction.

clue.text: Sound source of entertainment worth both its successors put together

definitions.text: Sound source of entertainment worth both its successors put together

parts.words: Sound source of entertainment worth both its successors put together
parts.note: an old gramophone record named for its speed, which was replaced by the 33 rpm album and the 45 rpm single, which add up to it

explanation.surface: An old music format is worth its two successors combined.
explanation.walkthrough: 33 + 45 = 78: the 78 rpm shellac record was followed by vinyl LPs at 33 and singles at 45.
explanation.definitionFit: A seventy-eight is a shellac gramophone record played at 78 revolutions per minute.
